target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosure details DCAI cost of sales decreases driven by lower server sales volume and inventory reserve adjustments. The search for a 2025 counterpart with matching specific drivers (DCAI cost of sales changes, lower server volume, inventory reserve impacts) yielded no exact match. The closest hit, intc_2025_7_D032, discusses DCAI *operating income* changes driven by different factors (Gaudi AI accelerator charges, operating expense reductions) and compares 2024 to 2023, not 2024 to 2025. intc_2025_7_D029 discusses 2025 vs 2024 DCAI operating income, driven by headcount reductions and server unit costs, which is a different topic than the specific cost of sales driver mix in D046. Therefore, no equivalent disclosure describing the same specific DCAI cost of sales variance topic for 2024 vs 2025 was found.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA attribute changes in their core financial metrics for the Data Center/AI segment to a combination of revenue mix/volume shifts and inventory management actions. Intel specifically cites 'lower period charges from reserved inventory sell-through and lower reserves' as a driver for its cost of sales decrease, alongside product mix (Intel 7). Similarly, NVIDIA attributes its gross margin increase to 'Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions.' Both disclosures highlight that inventory-related cost adjustments played a significant role in improving or stabilizing their respective financial performance in the AI/Data Center sector.

sentences.text: ▪DCAI cost of sales decreased $661 million from 2022, primarily driven by lower server sales volume, lower sample costs, and lower period charges from the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower reserves taken in 2023. These cost of sales decreases were partially offset by higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 7 products sold in 2023.
Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
